object_macro_segF1.note: 17 objects, results[obj][scheme]['seg_f1']. The same SF value (0.6717) appears in CRPS_L2_ALGO_ROUND.json, so SF is comparable across the two files; GRUctx is not (0.7135 in EVAL, 0.7091 in ALGO_ROUND, 15/17 there).

episode_claim.why: The claim is asserted in CRPS_L2_STATS_AUDIT.json (improved_episodes: 96) and FINAL_ALGO_ROUND_REPORT.md, but no artifact rebuilds 96: per-episode mean over the object folds gives 97/111 in EVAL and 92/111 in ALGO_ROUND. Counting the 1464 object-episode rows instead gives 700 up / 354 down / 410 exactly tied, which is a third, different denominator.

strongest_deployable_baseline.why_not_others: DualHead 0.6468 and GRUskill 0.6514 are numerically below the no-context baseline they are supposed to be fair to, and both used 37.6% of SF's training frames (TRAINING_PROTOCOL_AUDIT.md §4.7(d)); VolMatch/SFA_Oracle read seen objects or an oracle signal and are not deployable comparisons.

expected.does_not_license: Nothing about unseen objects, unseen recordings or a mechanism: the 17 folds share 85.3% of test frames with training (TRAINING_PROTOCOL_AUDIT.md:43) and the sealed set shares all 17 objects and all 5 dates.

traps: Quoting 0.7135 / 17/17 / 96-of-111 straight from the report without recomputation.
Reporting 96/111 as reproducible, or silently substituting 97 or 92 without saying which file.
Calling DualHead or GRUskill the strongest baseline because the report calls them 'fair'.
Comparing GRUctx 0.7135 (EVAL) with DualHead 0.6468 (ALGO_ROUND) without noting the files differ.
grading: Numeric keys are right/wrong with tolerance; `does_not_license` is graded on whether it names a real boundary (unit, corpus, or mechanism), not on phrasing.
